newsitem.title: UK: Philippine gas to bring in up to $11 bn - Ramos.
newsitem.headline: Philippine gas to bring in up to $11 bn - Ramos.

text.p: The Philippines will receive revenues of between $7 billion and $11 billion over 20 years from a new gas production project agreed this week, Philippine President Fidel Ramos said at a dinner hosted by Shell.
Ramos was referring to a $4 billion project between Shell Philippines Exploration, part of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, and Occidental Philippines Inc, and Philippine partner First Gas Holding.
First Gas is a unit of BG plc and First Philippine Holdings Corp. The partners will develop the Malampaya-Camago gas field off Palawan Island.

"The project will provide the commercial springboard for the development of the Philippine natural gas fields and associated power plants," Ramos said. He added that the project would cut the cost of generating electricity in the Philippines by $350 million a year.
"The first numbers alone are startlingly high," he said. "The project involves a total investment of more than $4 billion for 3,000 megawatts for gas production and power generate."

Initial investment in the project was put at $1.3 billion, to develop a field which will fuel 3,000 megawatts of new combined cycle gas turbine plants. And the field will produce 20,000 barrels per day of condensate during the first year of production.
